description: Backend (main.py) + backend tests: add the VERIFY takeover tier for dangling cloud resources (CLOUD_RESOURCE_PATTERNS + CNAME-target detection path in check_takeover) and richer DNS reporting (dns_status field, full cname_chain, resolved derived from dns_status), and append dns_status as the 12th CSV column. All within the existing SSRF guard, bounded Semaphore, and _csv_safe neutralization. This feature establishes the JSON+CSV contract that FEAT-002 (frontend/README) depends on, so it comes first.
steps: Read /home/aravind/New-SEC/.agents/tasks/task-takeover-dns/context.json and this FEAT file FIRST. Then read main.py (TAKEOVER_FINGERPRINTS, SubdomainResult, resolve_dns, resolve_cname chain helpers, check_http, check_takeover, analyze_subdomain, _summarize, CSV_COLUMNS, download_csv) before editing.

Add CLOUD_RESOURCE_PATTERNS near TAKEOVER_FINGERPRINTS in main.py: a module-level list of (compiled anchored regex, provider_name) covering AWS ELB (*.elb.amazonaws.com, *.elb.*.amazonaws.com), AWS S3 (*.s3.amazonaws.com, *.s3-website-*.amazonaws.com, *.s3.*.amazonaws.com), CloudFront (*.cloudfront.net), Azure (*.azurewebsites.net, *.trafficmanager.net, *.cloudapp.azure.com, *.blob.core.windows.net), Heroku (*.herokudns.com, *.herokuapp.com), GitHub Pages (*.github.io), GCP (*.storage.googleapis.com, *.appspot.com), Fastly (*.fastly.net). Add helper _match_cloud_resource(target) -> Optional[str] returning provider name or None (lowercase, strip trailing dot; anchored match to avoid substring false positives).

Add resolve_dns_detailed(host) -> tuple[list[str], str] returning (ip_addresses, dns_status) with dns_status in {RESOLVED, NXDOMAIN, NO_ANSWER, SERVFAIL, TIMEOUT, ERROR}. Prefer a dig-based status signal when dig is available (NOERROR+A -> RESOLVED, NOERROR no-A -> NO_ANSWER, NXDOMAIN -> NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL -> SERVFAIL, timeout -> TIMEOUT); fall back to socket.getaddrinfo with best-effort mapping (gaierror host-not-found/EAI_NONAME -> NXDOMAIN, socket.timeout -> TIMEOUT, else ERROR) and document the stdlib limitation in a comment. Run in executor like the existing resolver. Keep resolve_dns working (keep it or delegate to the detailed fn). Add a module comment documenting the HIGH > VERIFY > MEDIUM > LOW > NONE ordering (weights HIGH=4,VERIFY=3,MEDIUM=2,LOW=1,NONE=0).

Add resolve_cname_chain(host) -> list[str] (dig-first via _dig_cname logic, socket fallback via _socket_cname) that follows multiple CNAME hops, bounded to a small max (e.g. 10) to avoid loops. Keep existing resolve_cname returning the FIRST hop unchanged. cname_chain[0] must equal the existing single-cname value.
Extend SubdomainResult TypedDict with dns_status: str and cname_chain: list[str]; update the takeover_risk comment to 'HIGH | VERIFY | MEDIUM | LOW | NONE' noting the ordering.

Extend check_takeover signature to check_takeover(subdomain, cname, a_records, http_body, ptr_hosts=None, http_status=None, https_status=None, cname_chain=None) (new params keyword-defaulted so existing calls/tests still work). AFTER the existing fingerprint loop and BEFORE the final 'return NONE, None, None': if no HIGH/MEDIUM already returned, compute the final CNAME-chain target (prefer last element of cname_chain else cname), call _match_cloud_resource; if it matches AND a dangling HTTP signal holds (http_status or https_status in {404,503} OR both statuses are None while a cloud-resource CNAME exists), return ('VERIFY', provider, 'Dangling CNAME to <provider> (<target>) returning <status> — confirm the resource still exists and is owned by you before assuming it is safe.'). Never override an earlier HIGH/MEDIUM fingerprint return. Document the precedence (VERIFY only when the stronger check did not fire) in a comment. Use ONLY already-gathered data — issue NO new network request.

Wire new signals through analyze_subdomain in BOTH the invalid-hostname early-return SubdomainResult AND the main-path SubdomainResult: use resolve_dns_detailed for (ip_addresses, dns_status); set resolved = (dns_status == 'RESOLVED'); call resolve_cname_chain for cname_chain and keep cname = cname_chain[0] if cname_chain else existing resolve_cname result; pass http_status, https_status, cname_chain into check_takeover. Keep the _is_safe_public_ip SSRF guard and the shared asyncio.Semaphore exactly as-is; all new logic runs inside the existing 'async with sem' region and issues no new probe.
Update _summarize to add a 'verify' count (sum of takeover_risk == 'VERIFY'); keep existing resolved/alive/high_risk/medium_risk keys unchanged so the results endpoint exposes 'verify'.

Append 'dns_status' as the 12th entry of CSV_COLUMNS (end). In download_csv append _csv_safe(r['dns_status']) as the final cell; leave the first 11 columns/positions and their _csv_safe handling unchanged.

Add tests/test_takeover_verify.py: test_verify_dangling_elb_503 (cname_chain -> foo.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com, http_status=503, no body fingerprint -> risk VERIFY, service 'AWS ELB'); test_verify_does_not_override_high (existing body-fingerprint match still returns HIGH); test_cloud_resource_healthy_200_not_verify (cloud-resource CNAME with http_status=200 -> not VERIFY).

Add tests/test_dns_status.py (monkeypatch the resolver, offline): test_dns_status_nxdomain (-> 'NXDOMAIN' and resolved False), test_dns_status_resolved (A records -> 'RESOLVED' and resolved True), test_dns_status_no_answer (CNAME-only/no A -> 'NO_ANSWER'), test_cname_chain_multi_hop (multi-hop chain captured; first element equals the single cname).

Update tests/test_api.py::test_download_csv_header and tests/test_security.py::test_csv_download_neutralizes_injection to the new 12-column header (ending ...,takeover_detail,dns_status); assert dns_status appears and _csv_safe neutralization still applies to the new field. Ensure tests/test_api.py::test_full_flow passes with SubdomainResult now including dns_status/cname_chain (fake result sets them). Add an SSRF regression (extend the existing monkeypatch-based test) asserting VERIFY detection on a private-IP host issues no new probe.
acceptance_criteria: main.py imports cleanly: .venv/bin/python -c 'import main' succeeds and main._match_cloud_resource('foo.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com') == 'AWS ELB' while main._match_cloud_resource('example.com') is None.

'dns_status' and 'cname_chain' are in main.SubdomainResult.__annotations__, and main.CSV_COLUMNS == ['subdomain','ip_addresses','cname','http_status','https_status','sources','resolved','alive','takeover_risk','takeover_service','takeover_detail','dns_status'].
check_takeover returns VERIFY for the ELB+503 no-fingerprint case (meet.* style), still returns HIGH for a body-fingerprint match, and does NOT flag VERIFY for a healthy HTTP 200 cloud-resource.
dns_status mapping tests pass (NXDOMAIN/RESOLVED/NO_ANSWER) with resolved derived correctly; cname_chain captures a multi-hop chain with cname_chain[0] equal to the single cname.

The full suite passes: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q (previous 109+ tests plus the new backend tests), with the 12-column CSV header and formula-injection neutralization on dns_status verified, and the SSRF guard regression confirming no new unguarded request from VERIFY detection.
findings:
Implemented in main.py + backend tests. Full suite: 130 passed (was 109+, +21 net new/updated). Contract details FEAT-002 (frontend/README) must match:

- CSV_COLUMNS (exact final 12-element list, order matters; dns_status appended 12th): ['subdomain','ip_addresses','cname','http_status','https_status','sources','resolved','alive','takeover_risk','takeover_service','takeover_detail','dns_status']. First 11 unchanged; download_csv applies _csv_safe to the dns_status cell.

- Summary key name: _summarize() now returns the additional key 'verify' (int count of takeover_risk=='VERIFY'); existing keys resolved/alive/high_risk/medium_risk unchanged. The /api/results/{job_id} response therefore exposes data.verify alongside data.high_risk/medium_risk/total. Frontend displayResults should source the VERIFY count from data.verify.

- Risk ordering (use everywhere): HIGH > VERIFY > MEDIUM > LOW > NONE. Numeric weights HIGH=4, VERIFY=3, MEDIUM=2, LOW=1, NONE=0. Frontend applySort riskOrder map should be { HIGH:4, VERIFY:3, MEDIUM:2, LOW:1, NONE:0 }; applyFilters needs a 'verify' case (r.takeover_risk === 'VERIFY'); riskBadge whitelist must add 'VERIFY' (amber/orange, between MEDIUM and HIGH).

- takeover_risk value set is now: HIGH | VERIFY | MEDIUM | LOW | NONE.

- dns_status value set (6 values): RESOLVED | NXDOMAIN | NO_ANSWER | SERVFAIL | TIMEOUT | ERROR. resolved boolean is derived as (dns_status == 'RESOLVED'). NOTE behavior change: resolved used to be bool(ip_addresses) or bool(cname); it is now strictly dns_status=='RESOLVED', so CNAME-only hosts (no A/AAAA) report resolved=False. The invalid-hostname early-return SubdomainResult sets dns_status='ERROR', cname_chain=[].

- cname_chain shape: list[str] (JSON array), additive. Ordered list of CNAME targets following multiple hops (dig-first, socket fallback, bounded by main.MAX_CNAME_HOPS = 10, loop-protected). cname_chain[0] == the existing single-hop `cname` field value; empty list [] when there is no CNAME. The single `cname` field is unchanged. Frontend may render the chain joined with ' -> ' (XSS-safe via escapeHtml, e.g. in a title) while keeping the single-cname text in the cell.

- VERIFY detail-message format (exact template): 'Dangling CNAME to <provider> (<target>) returning <status> — confirm the resource still exists and is owned by you before assuming it is safe.' where <provider> is the _match_cloud_resource() name, <target> is the lowercased trailing-dot-stripped final CNAME-chain target, and <status> is the HTTP status string ('404' or '503') when a gone-signal fired, else the literal 'no HTTP response' when both http_status and https_status are None (and no body). Note the em dash (—) between target and 'confirm'.

- _match_cloud_resource(target) -> provider name or None; providers emitted: 'AWS ELB','AWS S3','AWS CloudFront','Azure Web Apps','Azure Traffic Manager','Azure Cloud App','Azure Blob Storage','Heroku','GitHub Pages','Google Cloud Storage','Google App Engine','Fastly'. Patterns are anchored (full-host suffix), no substring false positives.

- VERIFY precedence detail: check_takeover returns HIGH/MEDIUM immediately on a confirmed body fingerprint; a service-match-without-body LOW is HELD and may be SUPERSEDED by VERIFY when the final CNAME-chain target matches a cloud resource AND the HTTP signal is 'gone' (http_status or https_status in {404,503}) OR there was no response at all (both statuses None and empty body). A live cloud resource (e.g. ELB returning 200 with a body) stays LOW (not VERIFY). VERIFY uses only already-gathered data (CNAME + statuses) and issues NO new network request, preserving the single-site SSRF guard. New check_takeover kwargs (keyword-defaulted, back-compatible): http_status=None, https_status=None, cname_chain=None.

- New main.py public functions FEAT-002/tests can rely on: resolve_dns_detailed(host)->(ips,status), resolve_cname_chain(host)->list[str], _match_cloud_resource(target)->Optional[str], CLOUD_RESOURCE_PATTERNS (list of (compiled_regex, provider)). resolve_dns(host) retained (delegates to resolve_dns_detailed, discards status) so legacy callers are unaffected; however analyze_subdomain now calls resolve_dns_detailed/resolve_cname_chain, so offline tests must monkeypatch THOSE (not resolve_dns) to control resolution.
